sar.narrative: Customer C07297 was the subject of an investigation regarding card C07297-K1, which exhibited activity consistent with an undocumented fraud pattern. Between 2016-11-21 and 2016-11-21, four online purchases were made on the card, each priced just under $500 to remain below a specific authorization limit. The total value of these transactions was $1906.07, representing the total exposure identified in this matter. This behavior aligns with authorization-threshold structuring, a pattern not among the five documented types but matching prior closed cases CC-3748, CC-3841, CC-3907, CC-4086, and CC-4124. The investigation was initiated by the cardholder's dispute of transaction T3476682 and the detection of a new device marker. Case HHG-006 resulted in an uncertain verdict with a fraud probability of 0.70, as the requested customer validation yielded no reply within the 24-hour window. The lack of customer response left the single unconfirmed signal unresolved, preventing a definitive conclusion despite the cardholder denying the charge. Related prior investigations reviewed as case memory included CC-0485, CC-0668, CC-0076, CC-0489, and CC-0683. The final actions taken included blocking the card, creating a case, filing a report, and escalating to an analyst. These measures were implemented because the cardholder denied the charge, triggering the block recommendation despite the probability remaining below the 0.85 threshold.
